prompt: A particle moves in a circular path at constant speed. Explain why the particle is accelerating, even though its speed does not change.

mark_scheme.criterion: States that velocity is a vector quantity having both magnitude and direction.
States that the direction of motion changes continuously, so velocity changes (producing acceleration).

hints: Explain what happens to the direction of motion as the particle moves around the circle.
solution: Velocity is a vector quantity that has both magnitude and direction. In circular motion, the direction of motion changes continuously, so the velocity changes. Because acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, the particle is accelerating.
teacher_walkthrough: Award 1 mark for identifying velocity as a vector with direction.
Award 1 mark for linking continuous change in direction to a changing velocity, which defines acceleration.
